Everyone is different of course but switching to a barefoot style of shoe helped significantly with my knee and ankle pain.
In what way did the new shoes alter your running?

Simply put, It reinforces a low impact strike which helps reduce the stress on joints caused by running.

The downside is that you are literally starting from ground 0 when transitioning to a minimalist shoe. Like couch to 5k transition, to prevent the likelihood of injury.

The short of it is that you run on the balls of your feet. This results in a significantly smaller impact than from the heel-strike that happens wearing regular runners, which in turn is much easier on the foot, ankle, and knee. You use some different muscles so it takes a while to build strength but I had a significant reduction in pain within 2 weeks of switching, and I've never looked back. Added bonus is I'll get at least 2 seasons out of a pair of VFFs, which are less than 1/2 the cost of the Nike Airs that I barely got a season out of.
